title: Causal credit assignment for long-horizon agents
definition: Which earlier actions actually changed the chance of eventual success?
motivation: Terminal rewards conflate useful actions with later failures.
existing_limitations: Explicit action-level counterfactuals are difficult when environment state cannot be restored.
possible_approaches: Compare matched restarts where feasible; otherwise report identification limits.
risks: Environment replay fidelity may dominate the estimate.

title: Adaptive credit assignment granularity
definition: When should credit be assigned by token, turn, tool call, or milestone?
motivation: Fine-grained evaluation is costly; coarse reward can obscure useful behavior.
existing_limitations: Existing methods make different granularity choices under different assumptions.
possible_approaches: Allocate evaluator calls to uncertain segments; compare equal-budget baselines.
risks: Verifier cost and bias may erase the gain.

title: Uncertainty-aware advantage estimation
definition: Can advantage estimates expose uncertainty from sparse or noisy feedback?
motivation: A single scalar advantage can hide uncertainty about causal contribution.
existing_limitations: The survey identifies weak intermediate verifiability and partial observability.
possible_approaches: Estimate intervals from repeated rollouts and calibrate against held-out outcomes.
risks: Repeated rollouts may not be independent.

title: Memory credit across sessions
definition: How should a policy credit a memory write that helps much later?
motivation: The reward may arrive after many sessions and retrieval decisions.
existing_limitations: Legacy memory entries await source verification; the link is a research lead.
possible_approaches: Track write, retrieval and outcome provenance across session boundaries.
risks: Cross-session evaluation protocols may be unstable.

title: Memory-to-policy consolidation
definition: When should learned experience become a policy update rather than stored memory?
motivation: Retrieval and parameter updates have different cost and adaptation behavior.
possible_approaches: Compare frozen-policy memory use with controlled fine-tuning under equal budgets.
risks: Separating consolidation effects from extra training is hard.

title: Non-stationary tools and environments
definition: How can an agent detect and recover from changed tools or environment rules?
motivation: Deployment interfaces and transition rules can drift.
existing_limitations: Existing benchmark work mainly evaluates a specified tool and policy setting.
possible_approaches: Version tools and inject controlled API failures or rule changes.
risks: Synthetic shifts may not represent real change.

title: Reward verifiability for open-ended tasks
definition: What evidence makes a success signal trustworthy in open-ended work?
motivation: A plausible answer may fail task constraints or leave state incorrect.
existing_limitations: Final-state checks cover some tool tasks but not every open-ended objective.
possible_approaches: Compare state-based checks, expert review and process checks on the same tasks.
risks: Human labels and automated checks can disagree.

title: Budget-aware agent exploration
definition: How should an agent trade success probability against token, tool and latency cost?
motivation: More search can improve decisions but consumes resources.
existing_limitations: Tree search illustrates multiple reasoning paths; explicit resource policies remain a separate question.
possible_approaches: Evaluate adaptive search against fixed-budget search at matched total cost.
risks: Cost accounting differs across providers and tools.

title: Active perception and adaptive planning
definition: When should an agent observe again rather than act from stale context?
motivation: Extra observations can correct beliefs but add latency and cost.
existing_limitations: The survey highlights partial observability, but this specific tradeoff needs targeted study.
possible_approaches: Randomize observation budget and measure errors under hidden-state changes.
risks: Observability controls may be hard to standardize.

title: Learning recovery from tool failures
definition: How should an agent adapt when tools time out, return bad data or change schema?
motivation: Real tool environments fail in ways fixed benchmarks may underrepresent.
existing_limitations: Reliable training examples with controlled failure modes are scarce.
possible_approaches: Inject reversible tool failures and compare recovery under equal rollout budgets.
cost_note: Curator estimate for small-model experiments; not measured.
risks: A policy may learn benchmark-specific retries rather than general recovery.

title: Cost-aware tool scheduling
definition: Can a policy choose tools under success, token, API and latency budgets?
motivation: Real deployment requires more than maximizing task success alone.
existing_limitations: A single weighted score can hide severe trade-offs.
possible_approaches: Report success-cost Pareto curves with explicit hard constraints.
cost_note: Curator estimate for small-model experiments; not measured.
risks: Pricing and latency may vary across deployment settings.

title: Belief calibration under partial observability
definition: Do agent confidence estimates match the actual state of the environment?
motivation: Belief-based rewards can fail when the agent is confidently wrong.
existing_limitations: Current belief proxies may be self-referential and uncalibrated.
possible_approaches: Compare predicted state confidence with held-out observations and interventions.
cost_note: Curator estimate for small-model experiments; not measured.
risks: State labels may not be available in real environments.

title: Trajectory reconstruction in harnessed RL
definition: How can separate LLM calls become consistent training trajectories?
motivation: Real harnesses control tools, context compression and branching.
existing_limitations: Retokenization, merged samples and policy staleness can distort updates.
possible_approaches: Record call boundaries and compare loss-normalization schemes at equal budget.
cost_note: Curator estimate for small-model experiments; not measured.
risks: Training and deployment harnesses may diverge.

title: Memory and context budget optimization
definition: What should an agent retrieve, retain or discard under a fixed context window?
motivation: Memory management is itself a long-horizon action policy.
existing_limitations: Retrieval similarity does not measure downstream decision value.
possible_approaches: Evaluate memory actions on cross-session task success at fixed token budget.
cost_note: Curator estimate for small-model experiments; not measured.
risks: Benchmark-specific memory traces may not transfer.

title: Credit assignment in agent teams
definition: How should a team outcome be attributed to cooperating agents?
motivation: Subagents may contribute unequally and at different times.
existing_limitations: Team rewards obscure individual counterfactual contributions.
possible_approaches: Use controlled ablations of agent roles with fixed team budgets.
cost_note: Curator estimate for small-model experiments; not measured.
risks: Ablating one agent may change other agents’ behavior.
